input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds the Customer to a post-term non-compete of twenty-four months, worldwide ("in any territory"), covering "any product or service that competes with Vendor" — undefined scope with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (it expressly bars acquiring such products). That is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback on every material term: duration (24 months post-term vs. term-only/12 months), scope (any competing product vs. a named product) and carve-outs (none). It also directly conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. We propose deleting § 12.4, leaving § 12.3 to govern; if Copperleaf needs protection we can discuss the narrowed fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or businesses we may build, buy or sell, so we have deleted the 24-month, worldwide non-compete in § 12.4, which also directly contradicts § 12.3. If Copperleaf needs protection for a specific offering, we can discuss a narrow restriction limited to a named competing product during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month post-term worldwide non-compete binding Customer (§ 12.4).
